headline: Town committees finalized recommendations and outreach for the upcoming Special Town Meeting, focusing on contentious trail, golf course, and zoning warrant articles.
synopsis: Ahead of the October 17 Special Town Meeting, Southborough boards finalized their positions and presentations on key warrant articles. The Community Preservation Committee and Trails Committee advanced the full funding proposal for the Peninsula Trail footbridge, while the Advisory Committee finalized reports opposing the bridge cost and golf course irrigation funding. The Advisory Committee voted to recommend $240,000 for municipal water connections near the Parkerville landfill and finalized an unfavorable recommendation on two-family zoning amendments. Separately, the Zoning Board of Appeals voted to support the two-family zoning article as drafted, and the Select Board reviewed initial findings from a town governance study.

highlights.title: Peninsula Trail bridge funding advanced to Town Meeting as drafted
highlights.why: The Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to advance Article 4 as printed without cutting contingency funds. The project carries a maximum cost of $428,550, which the Advisory Committee unanimously opposes due to high per-foot construction costs.

highlights.title: Advisory Committee recommends $240,000 water connection near landfill
highlights.why: The committee voted 6-0 to recommend Town Meeting approval to extend a water main and connect two homes in the testing area of the closed Parkerville Road landfill. Funding will come from water retained earnings, and the town will pay for the service lines into the houses.

highlights.title: Zoning Board supports two-family housing warrant article
highlights.why: The board voted unanimously to move the two-family zoning amendment forward as drafted without removing lot requirement language. In contrast, the Advisory Committee finalized an unfavorable recommendation on the article over concerns about house flipping, septic capacity, and lot sizes.

highlights.title: Golf Committee funds informational campaign for irrigation project
highlights.why: The committee authorized up to $500 to print flyers explaining the $1,087,296 golf course irrigation project ahead of Town Meeting. The project requests $433,546 in additional Community Preservation Act funds, which the Advisory Committee opposes on the grounds that the golf course was meant to be self-sustaining.

highlights.title: Select Board reviews town governance study findings
highlights.why: Consultants presented an analysis comparing Southborough's governance model to peer towns, noting the town currently has 68 committees. The review examined the town manager structure, charter considerations, and committee oversight.
